Biophys. Biochem. Cytol. 1: 59–68), Brenner, Jacob & Meselson (13 May 1961 Nature 190: 576–581), Crick, Barnett, Brenner & Watts-Tobin (30 December 1961 Nature 192: 1227–1232), and Nirenberg & Matthaei (October 1961 PNAS 47: 1588–1602) maps DNA (A, T, C, G) → mRNA (A, U, C, G) → 64 triplet codons (4³ = 64) → tRNA adaptors → 20 amino acids on the ribosome, led by UUU = Phenylalanine (39,800 cpm vs 70 cpm background).

teach_overlay.label: CENTRAL DOGMA (DNA → MRNA → RIBOSOME → PROTEIN), 4³ = 64 TRIPLET CODONS & NIRENBERG-MATTHAEI POLY-U (39,800 VS 70 CPM)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Central Dogma (DNA → mRNA → ribosome → protein) & 64-triplet genetic code table on period paper showing 4 bases read in 1-letter (4), 2-letter (16), vs 3-letter (4³ = 64) words for 20 amino acids, and Nirenberg & Matthaei's 27 May 1961 poly-U experiment (39,800 cpm 14C-phenylalanine incorporation vs 70 cpm control)
teach_overlay.scale: if you read the four letters of DNA one at a time, you only get four words; in pairs, you only get sixteen — so life reads DNA in three-letter triplets, giving sixty-four possible words to spell twenty amino acids and punctuation stops
